description: Storms nest in the crystals on its shell. It crosses a valley in a lifetime, thunder rolling in its wake.
lore: No one in that valley gives a distance in miles. They say: as far as the shellback, or a day past it, or it was at the alders when I woke and it is at the beck now, so work it out yourself. It walks one line at the pace of a shadow coming off a wall and has never once turned aside. The crystals are the weather's business rather than its own — sit against the shell through a storm and you feel them go off through the stone, and the animal does not change its footing. It is not the [[monsters/stone_turtle|one on the gorge crossing]], which was never anywhere and never an animal. This one woke here like everybody, out of some country that had real weather in it.

The woman who kept the fire at the head of that valley walked out to it every eighth day, for a stretch of years she had long stopped counting, and talked the whole way round it. The rota. Who had come. Who was going soft. What the wind was doing to the alders. A telling wants somebody listening, and there was no one else left on that road, and she had decided the shellback would do — she said so to anyone who raised it, in the tone of a person who has already had the argument with herself and won it.

She went [[lore/the_quiet|Quiet]] out there, in the ordinary way, slowly. The ground where the shellback lies up is still the sharpest ground in the valley: grass with edges on it, stones that have not shifted through a Turn, while the far end of the same road has gone the colour of an idea. The tortoise has made perhaps two fields since. It did not stop for her and it does not carry one word she said. What holds that ground is not the tortoise. It is four hundred years of somebody standing next to it, talking.
gm_notes: The clock is the whole point: a creature whose crossing outlasts the people who measure by it, and which cannot return a relationship anyone has with it. Her tellings held that ground and are still holding it, which the valley reads as the animal being lucky — leave that misattribution in place. Do not name her; onomastics are unsettled, and the record is stronger with a role and no name. Nothing here is bound to a stone.
